title: the bus never bounces mail a wired shim is still taking
intention: The bus never bounces mail that a wired shim is still taking: no_receiver waits out a take under way before it judges the envelope undeliverable.
why: Measured 2026-11-16: two scratch buses bounced the first inspect ask to codemother with "codemother's shim could not take the envelope — it cannot wake a device to receive it", 0.24 s and 0.59 s after bus start, with her hooked and wired before and after. serve's backlog thread called no_receiver on that envelope while she was still taking it under her lock. This is 69cd150dc116 (n=5), which red-seals proofs and holds aa3e, 149b and 62a8.
traces_to: Law 8: a seal red on load, not code, is one a peer cannot lean on. Law 7: a bounce of mail being delivered is a false record.
how: no_receiver in server.py holds the addressee's lock (_holding) after hold_name finds a shim, then re-checks _still_waiting. A red-first proof runs return_the_backlog while a wired shim's device is blocked mid-take.

clauses.claim: the backlog pass, run while a wired shim's device is still taking an envelope, returns nothing to the sender, and the envelope is taken once and receipted
backlog mail to a name no shim answers still comes back to its sender in the same pass

decisions.text: D1: no_receiver waits on the addressee's shim lock before it judges the envelope still waiting.
D2: a red-first proof, one tooth per clause, over BusDevice.scratch with a shim whose device blocks mid-take.

measured.saw: bounce lines at 07:20:04.745Z (bus started 07:20:04.501Z) and 07:20:14.552Z (started 07:20:13.963Z): sender cc, verb inspect, hook_before/after and wired_before/after all true, shim CodeMotherShim
